title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps

epigraph.quote: A low headline cash multiple is only cheap if the receivables convert without a write-down and the flagship contracts avoid a legal reset.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Discipline

web_blocks.html: At the November 20, 2026 close of $341.50 (TradingView: $341.77), General Dynamics carries a $92.28 billion market cap [13][14]. That reflects 270.22 million basic shares (273.8 million diluted) [13][27]. Enterprise value stands at $96.92 billion [13]. That figure reconciles exactly to the Q3 2026 balance sheet: $92.28 billion equity plus $7,016 million debt and $2,014 million leases, less $4,388 million cash [13][27]. On trailing results, GD trades at 20.08x P/E ($17.01 TTM diluted EPS) and 18.07x Forward P/E [13]. Shares also trade at 15.97x P/FCF (6.26% FCF yield), 14.23x EV/EBITDA, 1.71x EV/Sales, and 3.38x P/B ($101.00 book/share) [13]. The trailing dividend yield is 1.84% ($6.27 TTM; 38.83% payout) [13].

Why is GD down 14.62% from its $400.00 peak despite $220.3 billion in backlog and 13.22% ROIC [12][13][14]? Pass 1's footnote audit explains the discount. First, Q3 2026 Note J disclosed August 2026 SEC, DOJ Civil Division, and DoW OIG subpoenas into Electric Boat submarine cost recording and reporting [27]. Second, 49.3% ($108,543 million) of total backlog is unfunded, including $99,576 million in Marine Systems [27]. Meanwhile, FY2027 appropriations sit under a Continuing Resolution expiring December 11, 2026 [22][27]. Third, Marine's 7.9% Q3 margin benefited from a Virginia Block IV adjustment and $137 million in 9M EAC uplifts ($44 million in Q3) [27]. Those timing items mask cost friction across 42.9% ($5,985 million) fixed-price Marine revenue [27]. Fourth, net unbilled receivables expanded to $8,906 million, including $1.2 billion on an international tracked-vehicle deal with a Note B risk warning [27]. At the same time, Technologies holds $14,515 million of GD's $20,849 million goodwill without a quantitative test since Q4 2022 [27]. Add Combat Systems' -$203 million 9M U.S. vehicle drop after M10 Booker, Gulfstream Israel supplier delays, and Novakovic's 45,353-share Form 4 sale [27][29][31]. Together, those filings prove the 16.0x P/FCF tag reflects real risk rather than blind market neglect [13][27].

web_blocks.caption: Stress-Tested Reverse DCF & Scenario Valuation (CMP = $341.50, EV = $96.92B, WACC = 8.8%)
rows: Tempered by Dec 11 CR funding risk, DoD shipbuilding schedules, and Combat U.S. vehicle contraction [22][27].
Models persistent 7.5%–8.2% Marine ceiling under 42.9% fixed-price mix [27].
Adjusts for $8.91B unbilled receivables and $1.2B+ shipyard capex [27].
Includes +30 bps governance and Electric Boat subpoena risk premium [27].
Probability-weighted charge across Note J probes, Note B $1.2B deal, and Tech goodwill [27].
Zero margin of safety at CMP; Base Case implies 18.8x FY27E EPS ($18.90) [13].
web_blocks.takeaway: An 8.8% WACC and $3.5B legal, unbilled, and goodwill haircut yield a $355.00 Base Case fair value. That leaves +3.95% upside from $341.50 and weak cushion against $245.00 stressed Bear risk.

web_blocks.caption: Defense & Aerospace Peer Valuation Matrix (Same-Session Snapshot, Nov 20, 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: GD trades at 18.07x Forward P/E and 15.97x P/FCF with 13.22% ROIC, yet sits in Stage 4 alongside NOC (17.90x Fwd P/E, 19.82x P/FCF) and RTX (23.44x Fwd P/E, 27.01x P/FCF) [13][17][18][24]. By contrast, Lockheed Martin (LMT) trades cheaper at 16.98x Forward P/E and 13.24x EV/EBITDA with 21.31% ROIC and confirmed Stage 2 structure [16][23]. Pure-play shipbuilder HII and Cessna parent Textron provide direct segment comparables for Marine and Gulfstream [19][20].

web_blocks.the_number: $355.00 per share Base Case intrinsic value (+3.95% vs. $341.50 CMP; $336.00 probability-weighted 12-month expected value).
web_blocks.how_calculated: We discount 10-year unlevered free cash flows at an 8.8% WACC and 2.75% terminal growth (16.0x Year-10 EV/FCF). We then subtract $4,642 million of lease-adjusted net debt and a $3,500 million risk haircut across 273.8 million diluted shares. We cross-check with Sum-of-the-Parts: three defense units (~$4.1B EBIT) at 12.5x EBIT ($51.25B) plus Aerospace (~$2.13B EBIT) at 19.0x EBIT ($40.50B) equal $91.75B gross EV. Subtracting $4.642B net debt and $3.50B contingency leaves $83.61B equity value, or $305.36 per share (reaching ~$333–$356 per share only at 13.0x–14.0x Defense and 20.0x–21.0x Aerospace ex-haircut).
web_blocks.the_inputs: FY2026E revenue midpoint is $56.65B ($56.5B–$56.8B guide), with 5.3% 10-year CAGR, 10.7% terminal EBIT margin, 96% FCF conversion, and a 16.5% tax rate. Balance-sheet inputs use $4,388M cash, $7,016M debt, and $2,014M leases. We apply a $3.50B haircut ($12.78/sh) for Note J subpoenas, Note B $1.2B unbilled risk, and $14.52B Technologies goodwill [13][27].
web_blocks.the_range: Bear Case is $245.00 (-28.26% vs. CMP): stressing Base FY27E EPS ($18.90) by -$1.16/sh for annualized EAC unwind ($183M) and a -100 bps Marine margin reset (-$381.4M EBIT, -$318.5M after 16.5% tax) yields $17.74/sh stressed EPS; at 14.5x ($257.23/sh) less the incremental $4.0B ($14.61/sh) Bear charge ($7.5B Bear vs. $3.5B Base) implies $242.62/sh (rounded to $245.00). Base Case is $355.00 (18.8x FY27E EPS). Bull Case is $425.00 (21.0x FY27E EPS if subpoenas clear, CR passes, and Gulfstream exceeds 15.5% margins).
web_blocks.if_off: If DOJ and SEC close the Electric Boat review with zero clawback and Marine holds 8.5%+ ex-EAC margins, removing the $3.5B haircut lifts fair value by ~$13/sh toward $368–$390. Conversely, a False Claims Act settlement or $1.2B tracked-vehicle write-down pulls fair value toward $245–$305.

web_blocks.title: FCF Yield & Balance Sheet Quality Audit (15.97x P/FCF at $341.50)
paragraphs: On the surface, 15.97x P/FCF (6.26% yield) looks attractive after $4,827 million in 9M 2026 FCF ($5,745 million CFO less $918 million capex) [13][27][28]. Yet cash quality carries three caveats. First, net unbilled receivables grew +$526 million YTD to $8,906 million while 9M EBIT absorbed $137 million of net EAC catch-ups [27]. Second, GD funded $500 million into pensions in Q3 and faces $2,250 million of 2027–2028 debt maturities beside a $4 billion March 2027 credit line [27]. Third, consensus price targets ($416.52) still embed pre-subpoena Marine margin expansion that Q3 2026 filings do not support [13][27].

web_blocks.html: Historical Bands & Asymmetry Failure: Across FY2016–FY2025, GD traded between 14x and 22x earnings, averaging 17.5x–18.5x forward EPS [9][13]. At $341.50 (18.07x forward P/E), shares sit near their historical midpoint rather than at a distressed multiple [13]. With Base Case fair value at $355.00, even a pullback to the $339.20 support band top offers just $15.80 upside against $24.20 risk to $315.00. That 0.65:1 support reward-to-risk ratio fails our 1.50:1 minimum hurdle, forcing a clean REJECTED verdict.

What Changes the Valuation Call: A reset below $295.00–$310.00 (~15.6x–16.4x Base FY27E EPS of $18.90) reopens valuation math. Alternatively, clean closure of the Electric Boat subpoenas alongside an 8.5%+ Marine margin run-rate would lift support R:R back above 1.50:1.

book_paragraphs: Now that our price-blind audit in Chapters 1 through 6 has surfaced every balance-sheet footnote and legal subpoena, we open the live market ledger for November 20, 2026. General Dynamics closed at $341.50 on Finviz and $341.77 on TradingView, giving the company a $92.28 billion equity market value and a $96.92 billion enterprise value.

Let us walk carefully through how that $96.92 billion enterprise value reconciles to the Q3 2026 balance sheet. Take the $92.28 billion equity value, add $7,016 million of total funded debt and $2,014 million of balance-sheet lease liabilities, and subtract $4,388 million in cash. The exact total is $96.92 billion. At that price, you are paying 20.08 times trailing earnings, 18.07 times forward earnings, 15.97 times free cash flow, and 14.23 times EBITDA, alongside a 1.84 percent dividend yield.

On a quick screen, 16 times free cash flow for a contractor with $220.3 billion in backlog and 13.22 percent return on invested capital looks tempting. Yet an institutional analyst never stops at the headline multiple. You have to ask why the market knocked the stock down 14.6 percent from its $400 peak, and whether that discount actually covers the newly uncovered risks.

Start with the four new shadows inside the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q. First, Note J revealed August 2026 subpoenas from the SEC, the DOJ Civil Division, and the Department of War Office of Inspector General examining Electric Boat's submarine cost recording and financial disclosures. Second, 49.3 percent of headline backlog—$108.5 billion—is unfunded while Congress operates under a Continuing Resolution expiring December 11, 2026.

Third, Marine Systems' 7.9 percent Q3 margin benefited from a favorable Virginia Block IV completion adjustment across 42.9 percent fixed-price nine-month revenue, while consolidated nine-month profits included $137 million of favorable estimate-at-completion catch-ups. Fourth, net unbilled receivables climbed to $8,906 million, including $1.2 billion on an international tracked-vehicle contract carrying an explicit variable-consideration impairment warning.

Look closely at why that trailing free cash flow yield needs an adjustment. Over nine months, GD generated $5,745 million of operating cash flow and spent $918 million on capital expenditures, leaving $4,827 million in free cash flow. That equates to a 6.26 percent trailing FCF yield, yet unbilled receivables consumed $526 million year to date, GD funded $500 million into pension plans during Q3, and $2,250 million of fixed-rate debt matures between April 2027 and May 2028 right behind a $4 billion credit facility expiring in March 2027.

When we rebuild our 10-year Discounted Cash Flow model cleanly without anchoring to prior targets, those realities shift the math. We lift our discount rate by 30 basis points to an 8.8 percent WACC to price legal and governance risk, moderate 10-year revenue growth to 5.3 percent, cap terminal EBIT margins at 10.7 percent, and normalize free cash flow conversion at 96 percent with a 2.75 percent terminal growth rate.

We then subtract $4,642 million of lease-adjusted net debt and a $3.50 billion probability-weighted risk haircut—equal to $12.78 per share across 273.8 million diluted shares—covering the Electric Boat subpoenas, Note B unbilled receivables exposure, and $14.52 billion of Technologies goodwill that has not faced a quantitative test since Q4 2022. That clean model yields a Base Case intrinsic value of $355.00 per share.

Run a Sum-of-the-Parts check and you get an even clearer floor. Value the three defense segments—Marine Systems, Combat Systems, and Technologies—generating roughly $4.1 billion of normalized EBIT at 12.5 times, or $51.25 billion. Value Gulfstream Aerospace at 19 times its ~$2.13 billion EBIT, or $40.50 billion. Together that is $91.75 billion of gross enterprise value; subtracting $4.642 billion of lease-adjusted net debt and $3.50 billion for contingencies leaves $83.61 billion of equity value, or $305.36 per share. Reaching $333 to $356 per share on SOTP would require lifting defense to 13x–14x and Aerospace to 20x–21x with zero legal haircut.

Historical valuation bands reinforce the same caution. Across FY2016 through FY2025, General Dynamics traded between 14 times and 22 times earnings, averaging roughly 17.5 to 18.5 times forward EPS. At $341.50, or 18.07 times forward earnings, the stock trades right at its ten-year midpoint rather than at a crisis discount.

Peer multiples confirm there is no hidden bargain here either. In the same November 20 snapshot, Lockheed Martin trades at 16.98 times forward earnings and 13.24 times EV/EBITDA with a far higher 21.31 percent ROIC and a healthy Stage 2 chart. Meanwhile, Northrop Grumman at 17.90 times forward earnings and RTX at 23.44 times forward earnings are both trapped in Stage 4 alongside General Dynamics, while pure-play shipbuilder Huntington Ingalls and Cessna parent Textron show how sharply the market separates clean shipyard execution from cost-overrun noise.

Why does consensus carry a $416.52 average price target when our Base Case sits at $355.00? Most sell-side models extrapolate management's raised FY2026 guidance of $56.5 billion to $56.8 billion in sales and $17.20 to $17.30 in diluted EPS straight into 2027 without deducting any probability-weighted charge for the August 2026 Electric Boat subpoenas or the $1.2 billion tracked-vehicle unbilled balance. Our underwriting refuses to assume zero legal or working-capital friction until filings confirm it.

Now do the simple risk-reward math that separates disciplined underwriting from wishful thinking. At $341.50, our $355.00 Base Case offers only 3.95 percent upside. Meanwhile, stressing FY27E EPS from $18.90 down to $17.74 for EAC unwind and a 100-basis-point Marine margin reset at 14.5 times ($257.23), less the incremental $4.0 billion Bear legal and goodwill charge ($14.61 per share), puts our Bear Case at $245.00 ($242.62 unrounded)—28.3 percent below today's price. Even if you waited for a pullback to $339.20—the top of the technical band—against our $315.00 structural floor, you are risking $24.20 to make $15.80.

That 0.65-to-1 support reward-to-risk ratio fails our 1.50-to-1 minimum hurdle by a wide margin. Refusing to anchor to old targets is what protects capital here. Yesterday's $405 target assumed smooth Marine margin expansion and ignored federal subpoenas, Continuing Resolution funding cliffs, and $8.91 billion of unbilled receivables.

Today's honest $355.00 valuation shows the stock is simply not cheap enough to absorb those risks. Unless shares reset toward $295 to $310—or the SEC, DOJ, and DoW close the Electric Boat review with zero material clawback—new capital has no margin of safety at $341.50.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Notice how re-computing the DCF from scratch changes the answer. Once you model an 8.8% WACC, 10.7% terminal margins, and a $3.5B haircut for Electric Boat subpoenas and unbilled receivables risk, fair value drops from $405 to $355—turning a 16x FCF headline into an unattractive 0.65:1 risk-reward setup.
